messages:
hana: Quick RFC follow-up 1: we need a named "guardian" layer between controller and runtimes to arbitrate fallbacks and enforce budget caps. thoughts?
miguel: +1 on guardian. It should be lightweight, only mediate decisions and attest provenance. Not a heavy stateful engine.
tia: Important: guardian must know cost-budgets per-team so it can block expensive fallbacks that would blow committed capacity. We saw this in prod last month.
owen: Agree. Also guardian should support 'policy hints' from teams (latency-first, cost-first) and a global guardrail bucket that overrides hints when safety thresholds tripped.
hana: Design idea: runtime proposes action with metrics_signature, guardian evaluates policy+budget and either issues an "approved" or "veto". If veto, controller can escalate to manual review or forced override.
miguel: For speed, local runtime can still perform emergency hard-stops (safety tier). Guardian only gets involved for non-emergency fallbacks. That keeps fast-paths intact.
tia: Telemetry contract: runtimes stream compact_signatures every 5s: {ts, err_pct, p95_ms, sample_n, seq}. Guardian keeps rolling window for reconcile. Payload budget <1KB/canary.
overridebot: canary: guardian-probe id=gnrd-2026-03-22-09:12 size=3% region=us-east :satellite:
owen: Budget enforcement: guardian applies cost_rate_limit per-minute. If an approved fallback would exceed budget, guardian either recommends soft-fallback or tags request as "requires-approval".
hana: Soft vs hard semantics: soft = new sessions route away, hard = preempt & drain. Guardian should prefer soft when budget constrained. Teams can mark certain canaries as "safety-critical" to allow hard if necessary.
miguel: We also need a cohesive audit trail: every decision from runtime, guardian, controller, and manual reviewer gets a signed envelope and is recorded in the decision_log. Must be queryable by trace id.
tia: UX ask: Console should show live "budget burn" and a small explainer: why a fallback was blocked (budget, sample_count, guardrail). That saves pages.
owen: Failure modes: guardian outage -> fall back to default policy: local emergency allowed, non-emergency disabled (reject fallbacks) and create incident. So safest default on guardian loss is conservative.
hana: Conflict resolution: when local runtime issues immediate action and guardian later vetoes, controller should reconcile by either honoring guardian (if within reclaim_window) or creating a rollback ticket. Need monotonic decision ids for deterministic resolution.
miguel: For manifest, propose fields: guardian_mode: [opt-out, advisory, authoritative], budget_label, safety_flag. Example:
```yaml
canary:
  guardian:
    mode: authoritative
    budget_label: monthly-experiment-42
    safety_flag: false
    reclaim_window_s: 40
```
tia: Tests: add synthetic scenario where guardian blocks a costy fallback but local hard-stop triggers for a brief spike. Validate reconciliation path and audit.
owen: Observability: add cohesion_lag_ms, guardian_veto_count, budget_block_count. Alert if guardian_veto_count spikes unexpectedly.
hana: Security: guardian+controller comms mTLS + signed decisions. Manual overrides need two-person approval unless emergency safety.
miguel: Action items: 1) proto for decision_envelope + decision_log @miguel, 2) manifest extension PR @tia, 3) Console mockups for budget UX @owen, 4) chaos test for guardian outage @hana.
overridebot: guardian: gnrd-2026-03-22 verified probe complete at 09:15 :white_check_mark:
hana: I'll draft the addendum to the RFC with these guardian primitives. Thanks all. :memo:
